dataset_metadata.name: CALCE Accelerated Cycle Life Testing - LiCoO2 Pouch Cells (2018)
dataset_metadata.institution: Center for Advanced Life Cycle Engineering (CALCE), University of Maryland
dataset_metadata.citation: Diao, W., Xing, Y., Saxena, S., and Pecht, M. (2018). Evaluation of present accelerated temperature testing and modeling of batteries. Applied Sciences, 8(10), 1786. doi:10.3390/app8101786
dataset_metadata.funding: No external funding reported; supported by CALCE member companies and organizations

cell_info.electrolyte: LiPF6 salt mixed with organic solvent
cell_info.cell_notes: Charge cut-off voltage 4.4 V; discharge cut-off voltage 3.0 V. Electrolyte stated as LiPF6-salt mixed with organic solvent (paper.pdf, Case Study 2).

aging_modes.notes: Full factorial DOE: 4 temperatures x 2 charge cut-off C-rates x 3 discharge C-rates = 24 conditions. Most conditions have 8 cells; conditions 23 and 24 (60 °C, 2C discharge) have only 3 cells reported. EOL at 80% nominal capacity as shown in figures.

time_protocol.notes: Cycles run until ~1000 cycles or EOL. Checkup performed every 50 cycles. Rest of 5 min between charge and discharge half-cycles.

rawdata.known_issues: Conditions 23 and 24 (60 °C & 2C discharge) have only 3 of the planned 8 cells reported.

checkup.notes: Capacity measurement: standard charge profile followed by rest 5 min then standard discharge (0.7C to 3.0 V). Standard charge: 1.5C to 4.2 V, hold until 1C, then 1C to 4.4 V, hold until 0.025C.

notes: The dataset is associated with three publications: (1) Diao et al. 2019 J. Power Sources 435:226830 (accelerated cycle life and capacity degradation modeling); (2) Diao et al. 2019 Energies 12(15):2910 (knee-point algorithm); (3) Diao et al. 2018 Appl. Sci. 8(10):1786 (evaluation of Arrhenius model and decade rule). The charge protocol is a two-stage CC-CV: first stage 1.5C CC to 4.2 V then CV to 1C, second stage 1C CC to 4.4 V then CV to either C/5 or C/40 (stress factor 2). CALCE website also lists initial characterization data, continuous cycling data, and periodical characterization data as available downloads.
